For a 50-person Indian company, these are three currently available managed-TMC options. Exact programme fees are quote-based, so I would not treat any published fare as the total programme cost.

Provider	Current commercial offer	Cost to budget	Verify before paying
MakeMyTrip myBiz
	Corporate fares, GST invoices, expense tools; service fee negotiated in contract	Quote + GST; potentially 1.5% payment-gateway fee 
MakeMyTrip
	Service/transaction fees, cancellation/change charges, credit terms, GST-invoice coverage
EaseMyTrip EMTDesk
	Corporate fares, policy/approvals, expense management, dedicated 24/7 support 
EaseMyTrip
	Quote	Per-booking/management fees, refund timelines, credit limit, out-of-hours support
Thomas Cook India Corporate Travel
	Managed travel, self-booking, dedicated servicing/implant options, 24/7 emergency desk 
Thomas Cook
	Quote	Implementation/implant fee, transaction fees, SLA, cancellation/refund rules, minimum spend

Before signing: request a 12-month all-in quote showing airfare/hotel + TMC fees + GST + amendment/refund fees + payment charges, plus SLA and credit terms.

If this is for an India-based business hiring both engineers and customer-support staff, I’d shortlist these three:

Platform	Best for	Value	Main trade-off
Zoho Recruit	Best overall value	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	Per-recruiter pricing can add up
Freshteam	Small/early-stage teams	⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐	Less depth as hiring gets sophisticated
Keka	Hiring + HR/payroll together	⭐⭐⭐⭐	More expensive if you only need an ATS
1. Zoho Recruit — my default pick

Zoho is probably the best value if recruiting itself is the priority. Its Standard plan is listed at about ₹1,250/recruiter/month when billed annually, with 10 active jobs per recruiter, resume management, sourcing, assessments, interview feedback, career site, job boards and 50+ integrations. Enterprise is ₹2,500/recruiter/month annually and adds AI matching, automation and advanced analytics. 
Zoho
+1

Why I'd pick it: good fit for a mix of technical and non-technical hiring without forcing you into a full HRMS.

Watch: pricing is seat-based. If you have 5 recruiters, you're paying for 5 recruiter licenses even if hiring is uneven across the team.

2. Freshteam — best if you're still small

Freshteam is attractive when you want something simple and inexpensive to get running. Current India comparisons report a free tier for small teams, with paid functionality around the ₹1,500/month range. 
Zimyo - Best HR and Payroll Software

Why I'd pick it: easy setup, career site, resume parsing and interview scheduling without building a complicated recruiting operation.

Watch: I'd test it specifically against your engineering workflow. Once you're doing structured technical screening, multiple interview rounds, referrals, sourcing and reporting, you may outgrow it faster than Zoho.

3. Keka — best if HR is the bigger problem

Keka makes more sense if recruiting is only one part of what you need. Its value is the ATS → offer → employee onboarding → HR/payroll connection. Current Indian-market comparisons put Keka in the mid-market HRMS category rather than positioning it as the cheapest standalone ATS. 
Zimyo - Best HR and Payroll Software

Why I'd pick it: if you're simultaneously trying to clean up HR, attendance, payroll and onboarding.

Watch: don't buy a full HRMS just because its recruitment module looks good. If your only problem is "we need to hire 20 engineers/support people efficiently," Zoho is likely better value.

What I'd check before signing

For your particular mix of engineers + customer support, I would test these five things with real candidates:

Job-board integrations — especially Naukri, LinkedIn and whatever sourcing channels you actually use.

Technical screening — coding/assessment integrations, scorecards and interviewer feedback.

High-volume screening — resume parsing, knockout questions, AI matching and bulk rejection/email.

Hiring-manager experience — can a non-recruiter quickly review 20 candidates and submit structured feedback?

WhatsApp/email workflow — important for support hiring in India; check whether messaging requires another paid tool.

Also check candidate data retention/deletion, exportability, API access, and the cost of extra recruiter/hiring-manager seats before signing. Seat pricing is one of the biggest hidden costs as the recruiting team grows. 
Zoho
+1

My ranking: Zoho Recruit > Freshteam > Keka if you're primarily buying a recruiting platform. If you also need payroll/HRMS, I'd flip that to Keka > Zoho Recruit > Freshteam.
